{
  "project_id": "P-UK-FreeBreakfastClubs",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Delays or amendments in passing the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill could prevent establishing the mandatory legal duty on schools to offer free breakfast clubs.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Monitor legislative progress closely and ensure policy guidance aligns with statutory developments while encouraging voluntary early uptake.",
      "evidence": "the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill will place a duty on state-funded schools with primary-aged children to offer a free breakfast club"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Delays in obtaining timely approval and budget confirmation from HM Treasury could disrupt the April 2026 launch of the Year 1 national rollout.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Engage proactively with HM Treasury through regular business case updates and clear analytical budget projections.",
      "evidence": "These include timely approval and budget confirmation from HM Treasury, effective collaboration with the sector partners"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Delays in developing the internal CRM system MVP by November 2025 could impair processing school expressions of interest and first-line support.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Adopt agile delivery practices for the CRM MVP and establish manual fallback procedures for managing school applications.",
      "evidence": "develop a customer relationship management system internally, working towards a minimum-viable product from November 2025."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Closure of the National School Breakfast Programme in July 2026 could result in a gap in provision if participating schools are not successfully onboarded by September 2026.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Guarantee places for all NSBP schools early, simplify application steps, and coordinate directly with local authority networks.",
      "evidence": "ensure they do not have a gap in provision after the closure of the NSBP in July 2026."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Physical space constraints in primary schools could restrict their ability to accommodate all enrolled pupils for supervised breakfast provision.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Deploy technical estate advisers to assess facility capacity and help schools implement flexible room management solutions.",
      "evidence": "continuing contracts of technical estate advisers to test what schools can do to mitigate any space constraints."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Administrative burden or perceived financial shortfall could reduce school willingness to engage and join national rollout cohorts prior to statutory mandates.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Implement a simplified funding model with upfront start-up grants and provide direct self-service DfE support materials.",
      "evidence": "This should ease the burden and potentially increase willingness to engage and join the programme."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Upfront implementation costs combined with delayed attainment benefits could depress short-term value for money and benefit-cost ratio metrics.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Track early attendance and readiness metrics while conducting a comprehensive independent evaluation from 2026 to 2028.",
      "evidence": "costs are incurred upfront while attainment benefits only materialise after at least one year."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Insufficient availability of skilled staff and resources within DfE and the education sector could constrain national rollout delivery capacity.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Procure delivery support advisers via the education framework and deploy standard guidance toolkits across schools.",
      "evidence": "and the availability of skilled staff and resources, in both DfE and the education sector."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Regional labor market fluctuations exceeding standard area cost adjustments could cause operating budget shortfalls for participating schools.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Conduct periodic deep-dive funding reviews across cohorts and adjust regional cost formulas in subsequent financial years.",
      "evidence": "we apply an area cost adjustment to the funding to account for variations in the labour market."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Scaling national rollout to ~2,000 schools based on only one term's worth of learning from the early adopter scheme may introduce unforeseen operational failure modes.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Implement an iterative mixed-methods evaluation strategy and phase national rollout across two distinct school cohorts.",
      "evidence": "at the point of writing, this business case had one term's worth of learning."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Special education needs and disability settings may experience operational deficits if special school funding rates prove inadequate for higher care ratios.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Monitor special school cost structures through process evaluations and provide supplementary targeted local authority support.",
      "evidence": "At special schools, the funding rate is: £1,000 start-up grant, daily amount of £18.95, £3.23 for every child"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Ineffective or delayed data collection mechanisms could compromise monitoring of pupil attendance, participation rates, and compliance.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Initiate a commercial pilot for a call-centre to assist data collection and incorporate administrative tracking features into the internal CRM.",
      "evidence": "We will also start commercial processes to begin a call-centre pilot to support data collection."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Rising food prices and market inflation could cause school catering expenses to exceed the £1 per child daily variable funding rate.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Provide national advice on bulk procurement options and track unit catering costs through regular qualitative reviews.",
      "evidence": "plus £1 for every child that attends, regardless of characteristics or pupil need."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Inadequate coordination or funding delays for local authorities could lead to fragmented regional delivery support for primary schools.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Provide direct grant funding to local authorities and establish clear collaborative governance roles.",
      "evidence": "we will fund local authorities to support schools and the wider system to effectively deliver free breakfast clubs."
    }
  ]
}
